Context: The following is excerpted from a report by the American Library Association.
Title: Source F
Subtitle: American Library Association. The 2012 State of America's Libraries Report. American Library Association, April 2012. Web. 27 June 2014.
Content: Libraries persevere through cumulative, ongoing funding cuts

Overall, funding for public libraries continues to be suppressed in `text(2011)-text(2012)` budgets, with `5%` more states reporting decreased state funding for public libraries than in `text(2010)-text(2011)`. The cumulative impact of cuts to public library funding at the state and local levels since `text(2008)-text(2009)` has led public libraries to continuous budget-rebalancing and tough choices regarding continuity of services.
An online survey of chief officers of state library agencies in `text(November 2011)` elicited responses from `49` of `50` states and the District of Columbia. Among the findings:

:ibox:• `text(Twenty-three)` states reported cuts in state funding for public libraries from `text(2010)-text(2011)` to `text(2011)-text(2012)`. For `text(three years)` in a row, more than `40%` of participating states have reported decreased public library funding.
• Only `text(two)` states reported increased funding, but `text(one)` did so with a caveat. This state had experienced `text(two)` cuts the previous year, followed by a legislative action to reset its program to a lower funding level.
• `text(Seven)` states and the District of Columbia do not provide state funding.
• `text(Sixteen)` states reported there had been no change in funding from `text(2010)-text(2011)` to `text(2011)-text(2012)`.
• Only `text(nine)` states anticipated decreased funding for `text(2012)-text(2013)` — `21%` of last year's respondents, compared with `37%` of the previous year's. That may be the light at the end of the tunnel ... or a train coming.
